Starting with a set of n variables which are independent of each other and are called generators, the power set of this set has members which may be called atoms and are valuations of the n variables: a valuation can be considered to be a set of variables which are "true" under that valuation, or a conjunction of generators (such that variables not included in that set are included in negated form in the equivalent conjunction). Then the power set of the set of atoms yields a set of members which are the elements of the said field of sets. parados.text: Generally a screen or embankment to protect the rear of a position from enemy attack, from bomb splinters from behind, from enemy fire from a commanding height, or fire from flanking positions. In common English usage since World War II, the term "parados", particularly in trench warfare, has largely been discarded in favour of "rear parapet", which, etymologically speaking, is a contradiction in terms. In some contexts the term "rear traverse" is preferred, but no usage is exclusive.In fortifications that were enfiladed by enemy in positions commanding the fort, an internal parados could defilade the enemy, serving as physical protection and blindage. Usages of the term have varied inconsistently according to times and sources. Some sources use parados as a synonym for a traverse; some other sources represent parados as a special class of traverse and not necessarily at the back of any particular position. In trench warfare parados referred to a bank of earth or similar material behind the rear of the trench, opposite the parapet, affording protection from explosions and fragments when shells or bombs overshot the trench.

pseudocyst.label: medicine

pseudocystic.text: Of or relating to a pseudocyst; resembling a cyst.
pseudocystic.label: medicine

examples.text: pancreatic pseudocystography

pseudodata.text: Data that is artificially generated in order to test a program; test data.
pseudodata.label: computing

pseudodementia.text: A mild form of dementia from which the patient (often an elderly woman) may recover.
pseudodementia.label: medicine

pseudodemocracy.text: A government that holds elections but restricts civil liberties.
pseudodemocracy.label: politics

pseudodepression.text: The signs and symptoms of depression from a non-depressive, often organic aetiology.
pseudodepression.label: medicine

pseudodepression.text: Falsely depressed tracing, often on electrocardiography.
pseudodepression.label: medicine

examples.text: pseudodepression of the ST segment

pseudodevice.text: An entry in a file system that acts like a physical device without having the corresponding hardware.
pseudodevice.label: computing

pseudodextrocardia.text: The displacement of the heart to the right secondary to causes outside of it.
pseudodextrocardia.label: medicine

pseudodiarrhea.text: A condition of increased stool frequency (more than three times daily) with a normal daily stool weight of less than 300 g; it may accompany irritable bowel syndrome, hyperthyroidism, and anorectal disorders such as proctitis.
pseudodiarrhea.label: medicine

pseudodifferential.text: Describing an extension to differential calculus that deals with Fourier transforms and similar structures.
pseudodifferential.label: mathematics

pseudodifferential operator.text: An extension of the differential operator, used in the theory of partial differential equations and quantum field theory.
pseudodifferential operator.label: mathematics

pseudodimension.text: The largest cardinality (or infinite) of a set of points (in a function class) that can be shattered.
pseudodimension.label: mathematics

pseudodirectory.text: A virtual directory entry that does not represent a directory on the underlying file system on disk, instead being automatically generated to represent some other objects in the form of files (for example '/proc' in Linux).
pseudodirectory.label: computing

pseudodistance.text: A pseudometric having some characteristics of distance
pseudodistance.label: mathematics

pseudodiverticulosis.text: A condition characterized by the presence of pseudodiverticula (false diverticula that do not involve all layers of the intestinal wall), typically affecting the esophagus or colon.
pseudodiverticulosis.label: medicine

pseudodiverticulum.text: A pouch that extends along the wall of the intestine from a tumour of smooth muscle
pseudodiverticulum.label: anatomy

pseudodivision.text: Any of several methods of division that employ addition and shifting of digits.
pseudodivision.label: mathematics

pseudodomain.text: A nonexistent top-level domain that is assigned a meaning in certain specialized contexts.
pseudodomain.label: Internet

examples.text: The anonymity network Tor has a top-level pseudodomain .onion for hidden services, which can only be reached with a Tor client.

pseudodysentery.text: The occurrence of symptoms identical to those of bacterial dysentery, but not caused by the same microorganisms.
pseudodysentery.label: medicine

pseudoeffective.text: Having a nonnegative intersection product with every ample divisor and numerically eventually free if the intersection product with every positive divisor is non-negative.
pseudoeffective.label: mathematics

pseudoelection.text: A sham election; an election organized without any significant political choice or real impact on the results, often held in dictatorial regimes to feign the appearance of public legitimacy.
pseudoelection.label: politics

pseudoelement.text: An object in code that behaves like an HTML element but is not a true element.
pseudoelement.label: computing, Internet, Cascading Style Sheets

pseudoephedrine.text: A sympathomimetic alkaloid commonly used as a decongestant; a chemical compound, an isomer of ephedrine, with the formula C10H15NO.
pseudoephedrine.label: pharmacology

pseudoepileptic.text: paroxysmal and resembling an epileptic seizure
pseudoepileptic.label: pathology

pseudoepistaxis.text: Blood flow exiting the nostrils that is not due to a true nosebleed, that is, not truly originating from the nasal cavity; examples include blood coughed up through the airway and ending up in the nasal cavity, then dripping out.
pseudoepistaxis.label: medicine

pseudoerythrocytosis.text: A false appearance of elevated red blood cells caused by a reduced plasma volume rather than a true increase in red cell mass.
pseudoerythrocytosis.label: medicine, hematology

pseudoexacerbation.text: A sudden relapse in cases of multiple sclerosis, brought on by certain factors such as elevated temperature.
pseudoexacerbation.label: medicine

pseudoexfoliation.text: A form of exfoliation, especially in the eyes, in which the surface layer is not actually detached.
pseudoexfoliation.label: pathology

pseudofeculant.text: Having an appearance or smell similar to feces, usually due to the presence of anaerobic bacteria in an infected area.
pseudofeculant.label: medicine

pseudofever.text: A high body temperature that resembles, but is not in fact, a fever.
pseudofever.label: medicine

pseudofile.text: A file that does not represent a file on the underlying file system on disk, but instead is automatically generated to represent some other object in the form of a file (for example '/proc/cpuinfo' in Linux).
pseudofile.label: computing

pseudofinite.text: Of a field: both quasi-finite (perfect with a unique extension of every positive degree) and pseudo algebraically closed (every absolutely irreducible variety over the field has a point defined over the field).
pseudofinite.label: mathematics

pseudoform.text: A form that appears to be a legitimate word or linguistic unit but is not genuinely recognized as such within the language system.
pseudoform.label: linguistics

pseudofovea.text: An area of the retina in which an image is fixated (in a person with strabismus)
pseudofovea.label: anatomy

pseudofunctor.text: A mapping between categories that is just like a functor except that and do not hold as exact equalities but only up to coherent isomorphisms.
pseudofunctor.label: mathematics

pseudogestational.text: Of a sac, caused by an intrauterine buildup of fluid that has an appearance mimicking that of a gestational sac.
pseudogestational.label: medicine

pseudogland.text: A structure that has some resemblance to a gland
pseudogland.label: anatomy

pseudoglioma.text: inflammation of the eye that resembles glioma of the retina
pseudoglioma.label: pathology

pseudogout.text: A medical condition with symptoms resembling gout but caused by precipitation of calcium pyrophosphate crystals in the joints instead of monosodium urate crystals.
pseudogout.label: medicine

pseudographical.text: Having the appearance of graphics, though actually text-based.
pseudographical.label: computing

pseudographics.text: An approximation of graphics achieved through the use of text characters.
pseudographics.label: computing

pseudogroup.text: An algebraic structure having elements that are homeomorphisms between subsets of a space
pseudogroup.label: mathematics

pseudogroup.text: Any group of the extended periodic table containing lanthanides or actinides
pseudogroup.label: chemistry

pseudogynecomastia.text: An enlargement of the breast(s) due to excessive deposition of fat or skin, as opposed to “true gynecomastia” which results from the development of glandular breast tissue.
pseudogynecomastia.label: American spelling, medicine

pseudohallucination.text: A brief but vivid visual or auditory experience that is recognised by the experiencer as being unreal.
pseudohallucination.label: psychiatry

pseudohandle.text: A special value that can be treated as a handle (e.g. to identify a process) but is not a true handle.
pseudohandle.label: programming

pseudoheader.text: A simplified header used in the TCP and UDP protocols in order to calculate a checksum.
pseudoheader.label: Internet

pseudohermitian.text: Having the Hermitian properties except that the eigenvalues may be complex and the eigenvectors need not be orthogonal.
pseudohermitian.label: mathematics

pseudohyperaldosteronism.text: A condition where the body shows effects similar to excess aldosterone, such as high blood pressure, low potassium, and sodium retention. But aldosterone levels are actually normal or low.
pseudohyperaldosteronism.label: pathology

examples.text: Eating large amounts of liquorice can lead to pseudohyperaldosteronism.

pseudohyperkalemia.text: Falsely elevated serum potassium level, usually due to preanalytical error or blood cell disorders.
pseudohyperkalemia.label: medicine

pseudohypernatremia.text: A falsely elevated sodium level in the blood.
pseudohypernatremia.label: medicine

pseudohyperparathyroidism.text: A condition caused by the abnormal sensitivity to the parathyroid hormone.
pseudohyperparathyroidism.label: medicine

pseudohypertelorism.text: Any condition such as telecanthus that resembles, but is not in fact, hypertelorism.
pseudohypertelorism.label: anatomy

pseudohypertension.text: A falsely elevated blood pressure or blood pressure reading, often as a result of age-related arterial stiffness.
pseudohypertension.label: medicine

examples.text: In pseudohypertrophic paralysis, the muscles are apparently enlarged, but are really degenerated and replaced by fat.

pseudohypoaldosteronism.text: A medical condition that mimics hypoaldosteronism.
pseudohypoaldosteronism.label: pathology

pseudohypocone.text: A cusp, similar to a hypocone, that develops from a protocone (rather than the cingulum))
pseudohypocone.label: anatomy

pseudohyponatremia.text: A falsely low serum sodium concentration.
pseudohyponatremia.label: medicine

pseudohypoparathyroidism.text: A rare inherited disorder where the body does not respond properly to parathyroid hormone, causing low calcium and high phosphate levels despite high PTH in the blood.
pseudohypoparathyroidism.label: medicine

pseudohypoxemia.text: A spurious measurement of oxygen saturation of blood, giving a false appearance of hypoxemia; it can happen via technical problems (such as a malfunctioning pulse oximeter) or even when all technical details are correct but hyperleukocytosis or thrombocytosis is present and the testing method is blood gas analysis.
pseudohypoxemia.label: medicine

pseudohypoxia.text: A condition in which the symptoms of hypoxia are caused by metabolic complications, such as those associated with diabetes
pseudohypoxia.label: pathology

pseudoideal.text: The set of all lower bounds of the set of all upper bounds of a subset of a partially ordered set
pseudoideal.label: mathematics

pseudoinfarction.text: Any condition which imitates the characteristics of an acute myocardial infarction, especially in its pattern on an electrocardiogram.
pseudoinfarction.label: cardiology

pseudoinfection.text: The presence of pathogenic microorganisms in a host without an actual infection
pseudoinfection.label: pathology

pseudoinstruction.text: A command that resembles, but is not in fact, a machine instruction, such as a special directive or a command that is mapped to a sequence of real instructions.
pseudoinstruction.label: programming

pseudointerface.text: A software component that acts like a network interface but is not a true interface.
pseudointerface.label: computing

pseudointernuclear ophthalmoplegia.text: Slow adducting saccades not secondary to medial longitudinal fasciculus dysfunction. Usually caused by ocular myasthenia gravis.
pseudointernuclear ophthalmoplegia.label: medicine

pseudointersection.text: A set for which the number of elements that are not in the intersection (of two infinite sets) is finite.
pseudointersection.label: mathematics

pseudoinvasive.text: Being or relating to a pseudoinvasion.
pseudoinvasive.label: pathology

pseudoinverse.text: Any of several structures, similar to inverses, related to complex matrices
pseudoinverse.label: mathematics

pseudoinversion.text: An operation that approximates an inversion; A reversal of the ends while maintaining a constant central region.
pseudoinversion.label: mathematics

pseudoisotropic.text: That is isotropic in the three physical dimensions but not in some higher dimension
pseudoisotropic.label: mathematics

pseudolanguage.text: Something written or spoken that resembles language but is not a true language.
pseudolanguage.label: countable, uncountable

pseudolanguage.text: A means of describing an algorithm in human terms, without the use of a true programming language.
pseudolanguage.label: computing, countable

pseudoleukaemia.text: A condition in which there is a leukocytosis resembling that of leukaemia
pseudoleukaemia.label: pathology

pseudoleukocytosis.text: Transiently high leukocyte count (WBC count) that does not represent leukocytosis despite that it would seem to if interpreted in isolation (as opposed to the following of trends over serial measurements).
pseudoleukocytosis.label: medicine

pseudoleukopenia.text: Transiently low leukocyte count (WBC count) that does not represent leukopenia despite that it would seem to if interpreted in isolation (as opposed to the following of trends over serial measurements).
pseudoleukopenia.label: medicine

pseudolikelihood.text: An approximation to the joint probability distribution of a collection of random variables.
pseudolikelihood.label: statistics

pseudoline.text: A curve that shares certain topological properties with a line.
pseudoline.label: topology

pseudolobule.text: A structure, resembling a lobule, found in hepatic fibrosis.
pseudolobule.label: pathology

pseudolocking.text: The situation where a person has difficulty flexing or extending a joint, as though it were locked in place, but without any structural cause.
pseudolocking.label: medicine

pseudolongitudinal.text: Not actually longitudinal, but treated that way.
pseudolongitudinal.label: statistics, of a study or data

pseudolymphocytosis.text: Transiently high lymphocyte count that does not represent lymphocytosis despite that it would seem to if interpreted in isolation (as opposed to the following of trends over serial measurements).
pseudolymphocytosis.label: medicine

pseudomass.text: A constriction, typically of an airway, that has the appearance of a mass
pseudomass.label: pathology

pseudomeasure.text: A distribution that can be extended to a continuous functional.
pseudomeasure.label: mathematics

pseudomeatus.text: A deep indentation that appears to be an opening of the body
pseudomeatus.label: anatomy

pseudomedian.text: A measure of centrality for data sets and populations, which agrees with the median where the data are symmetric.
pseudomedian.label: statistics

pseudomembrane.text: A layer which resembles a membrane, especially one forming over a mucosal surface.
pseudomembrane.label: medicine, pathology

pseudomenses.text: Blood-tinged vaginal discharge in a female neonate, with an appearance resembling that of menses.
pseudomenses.label: medicine

pseudomenstruation.text: Uterine bleeding, or blood-tinged vaginal discharge, that resembles menstruation but is not associated with the typical endometrial changes thereof.
pseudomenstruation.label: medicine

pseudometric.text: Describing a generalization of a metric space in which the distance between two distinct points can be zero.
pseudometric.label: mathematics

pseudomoment.text: A numerical entity that combines the properties of moments and metrics
pseudomoment.label: mathematics

pseudomoniasis.text: Pseudomonas infection: a bacterial infection caused by any of various species of the genus Pseudomonas. Such infections occur in various host animals, especially certain fish; in humans immunodeficiency is typically a predisposing factor.
pseudomoniasis.label: biology, medicine

pseudomonoid.text: A structure similar to a monoid that supports associativity and an identity element, but does not include all the constraints that are required to qualify as a monoid.
pseudomonoid.label: mathematics

pseudomultiplication.text: Any of several methods of multiplication that employ addition and shifting of digits
pseudomultiplication.label: mathematics

pseudomycetoma.text: A mycosis of the skin resembling mycetoma
pseudomycetoma.label: pathology

pseudomyiasis.text: The presence of fly larvae in the body but without a true infestation, for example when larvae have been ingested with food.
pseudomyiasis.label: medicine

pseudomyotonia.text: An abnormally slow contraction and relaxation of muscles in response to mechanical or electrical stimulation but, unlike myotonia, it is silent on electromyography.
pseudomyotonia.label: pathology

pseudomyxoma.text: A cancer that has some characteristics of a myxoma
pseudomyxoma.label: pathology

pseudonation.text: An entity that falsely purports or is purported to be a nation.
pseudonation.label: politics

pseudoneurotic schizophrenia.text: A postulated mental disorder categorized by the presence of two or more symptoms of mental illness such as anxiety, hysteria, and phobic or obsessive-compulsive neuroses.
pseudoneurotic schizophrenia.label: psychiatry

pseudoneutropenia.text: Transient low neutrophil count that does not represent neutropenia despite that it would seem to if interpreted in isolation (as opposed to the following of trends over serial measurements).
pseudoneutropenia.label: medicine

pseudonodule.text: A benign structure similar to the nodule of a lymphoma.
pseudonodule.label: medicine

pseudonumerical.text: Being a factor-object of an algebraically numerical object.
pseudonumerical.label: mathematics

pseudonymization.text: The replacement of all data (in a database etc) that identifies a person with an artificial identifier or pseudonym.
pseudonymization.label: computing, law

pseudonymize.text: To depersonalize or anonymize (data); a procedure by which the most identifying fields within a data record are replaced by one or more artificial identifiers, or pseudonyms.
pseudonymize.label: computing, law

pseudoobstruction.text: Any of several conditions that prevent passage through the intestines / bowels without a physical obstruction
pseudoobstruction.label: pathology

pseudoparallelism.text: The execution of parallel processes on a unicore system.
pseudoparallelism.label: computing

pseudopatient.text: A person who poses as a patient so that research may be conducted or staff trained.
pseudopatient.label: medicine

examples.text: Most of the pseudopatients were falsely diagnosed with mental disorders.

pseudopenis.text: The enlarged clitoris of the female of various species including spotted hyena, binturong, and lemur.
pseudopenis.label: anatomy, zoology

pseudoperfect.text: Of a number, having proper divisors, some or all of which sum to the number itself.
pseudoperfect.label: mathematics

examples.text: The number 18 is pseudoperfect, because 3 + 6 + 9 = 18.

pseudoperiod.text: A solution function that is not technically periodic, but nevertheless displays repetitive behavior.
pseudoperiod.label: mathematics

pseudopharmaceutical.text: Any substance that only appears to, or is claimed to, have pharmaceutical effects.
pseudopharmaceutical.label: pharmacology

pseudopneumoperitoneum.text: A disturbance having the appearance of pneumoperitoneum
pseudopneumoperitoneum.label: pathology

pseudopolycythaemia.text: Uncontrolled and rapid cellular reproduction and maturation that causes proliferation or hyperplasia of all bone marrow cells.
pseudopolycythaemia.label: pathology

pseudopolynomial.text: A function where f(n+k) ≡ f(n) (mod k) for all integers n ≥ 0, k ≥ 1.
pseudopolynomial.label: mathematics

pseudopopulation.text: A subset of a population used in simulations
pseudopopulation.label: statistics

pseudoprime.text: An integer that possesses at least one characteristic of a prime number without actually being prime. The characteristic is typically chosen to make such "false primes" very rare.
pseudoprime.label: mathematics

pseudoprime.text: A Fermat pseudoprime; a composite integer n satisfying for some integer b such that b > 1.
pseudoprime.label: mathematics, specifically

pseudoproper.text: Describing any system that has some proper characteristics.
pseudoproper.label: mathematics

pseudoprotocol.text: Something that can be accessed in the manner of a protocol but is not in fact a protocol.
pseudoprotocol.label: computing

pseudopseudodementia.text: Organic brain disease, which features dementia presenting in a manner that mimics cognitive impairment secondary to a primary psychiatric disorder.
pseudopseudodementia.label: medicine

pseudopseudohypoparathyroid.text: Of, relating to, or having pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism.
pseudopseudohypoparathyroid.label: medicine

pseudopseudoseizure.text: An epileptic seizure manifesting in a manner that makes it prone to be misdiagnosed as a psychogenic nonepileptic seizure.
pseudopseudoseizure.label: medicine

pseudoptosis.text: A ptosis-like presentation with intact levator palpebrae superioris function.
pseudoptosis.label: pathology

pseudoquotient.text: A value in pseudodivision more or less corresponding to the quotient in normal division.
pseudoquotient.label: mathematics

pseudoradical.text: The intersection of the set of nonzero prime ideals of a ring.
pseudoradical.label: mathematics

pseudoradical.text: An atom or group within a molecule which behaves like a free radical due to high valence.
pseudoradical.label: chemistry

pseudoradicular.text: That seems to be associated with nerve roots
pseudoradicular.label: pathology, of pain

pseudorational.text: Able to be expressed as the convolution ratio of distributions with compact support.
pseudorational.label: mathematics

pseudoreflection.text: An invertible linear transformation of a finite-dimensional vector space such that it is not the identity transformation, has a finite (multiplicative) order, and fixes a hyperplane.
pseudoreflection.label: mathematics

pseudoreflexive.text: Of a verb: requiring the use of a reflexive construction when no reflexive action is actually taking place.
pseudoreflexive.label: grammar

pseudoreflexive.text: Inducing a topological isomorphism between the domain and its image.
pseudoreflexive.label: mathematics

pseudorelational.text: Having certain elements of a relational database.
pseudorelational.label: databases

pseudoremainder.text: A value in pseudodivision more or less corresponding to the remainder in normal division.
pseudoremainder.label: mathematics

pseudoreplicate.text: Any of a group of interdependent data that are mistakenly treated as independent.
pseudoreplicate.label: statistics

pseudoreplication.text: The exaggeration of the statistical significance of a set of measurements resulting from treating the data as independent observations when they are in fact interdependent.
pseudoreplication.label: statistics, especially in, biology, ecology

pseudorepresentation.text: Given a group and a commutative ring , a tuple of maps , where and , are a pseudorepresentation if they satisfy the relations one would expect if and were the diagonal entries of a two dimensional representation and if was given by .
pseudorepresentation.label: mathematics

pseudoresidual.text: The difference between the observed value and the median.
pseudoresidual.label: statistics

pseudorheumatoid.text: Seemingly rheumatoid but not (that is, clinically similar but pathophysiologically different).
pseudorheumatoid.label: biology, medicine

pseudorhombic.text: describing a structure that is almost rhombohedral
pseudorhombic.label: geometry, crystallography

pseudoring.text: Any of various variants of a ring.
pseudoring.label: mathematics

pseudoroot.text: A value that appears to be a root of a polynomial equation but that is not actually a root, such as one obtained when factors cancel out in the process of solving the equation.
pseudoroot.label: mathematics

pseudoroot.text: Any projection or nodule, such as the hypha of a fungus, that has a rootlike appearance without serving as an actual root.
pseudoroot.label: biology

pseudorosette.text: A structure resembling a rosette (tumor cell formation) that is not a true rosette.
pseudorosette.label: medicine

pseudosac.text: A (non-gestational) sac that develops in the uterus during an ectopic pregnancy
pseudosac.label: anatomy

pseudoscleroderma.text: Dermal fibrosis resembling scleroderma and occurring in conjunction with another disease.
pseudoscleroderma.label: medicine

pseudosclerosis.text: A disease resembling multiple sclerosis but in which the characteristic lesions are absent
pseudosclerosis.label: pathology

pseudoscutal.text: Of or relating to a pseudoscutum.
pseudoscutal.label: anatomy

pseudoselector.text: A kind of selector that identifies something not explicitly labelled in the document markup.
pseudoselector.label: computing, Internet, Cascading Style Sheets

pseudosequence.text: An apparent sequence used as a key in data compression
pseudosequence.label: mathematics

pseudospectral.text: Describing a class of numerical analysis methods related to spectral methods
pseudospectral.label: mathematics

pseudospectrum.text: A set containing the spectrum of an operator and the numbers that are "almost" eigenvalues.
pseudospectrum.label: mathematics

pseudosphere.text: A surface generated by rotating a tractrix about its asymptote; a tractricoid
pseudosphere.label: geometry

pseudosphere.text: Any of various surfaces with constant negative Gaussian curvature.
pseudosphere.label: geometry

pseudospinor.text: A pseudospin analog of a spinor.
pseudospinor.label: mathematics, physics

pseudospoofing.text: The use of a Sybil attack.
pseudospoofing.label: computing

pseudostate.text: A geopolitical entity which has some of the trappings of an independently-governed country or territory, but which lacks real independence and is not recognized as a self-governing political entity by the international community of nations.
pseudostate.label: politics

pseudostate.text: An entity that resembles, but is not in fact, a state in a state machine or similar.
pseudostate.label: computing theory

pseudostatement.text: A construct resembling a statement that is not a true statement.
pseudostatement.label: programming

pseudostatus epilepticus.text: An episode of prolonged seizure which presents similarly to status epilepticus, but is of nonepileptic (and often psychogenic) origin.
pseudostatus epilepticus.label: medicine

pseudostoma.text: A group of cells resembling a stoma, but without any true aperture among them.
pseudostoma.label: anatomy

pseudostreaming.text: The seeking of a portion of a streamed video that has not yet been downloaded
pseudostreaming.label: Internet

pseudosyllogism.text: A false syllogism, one that is not logically coherent.
pseudosyllogism.label: logic

pseudosylvian.text: Describing an extension of the lateral sulcus on each hemisphere of the brain
pseudosylvian.label: anatomy

pseudosyncope.text: A condition clinically similar to syncope but not truly syncopal in nature, being caused psychogenically; thus, apparent fainting but without concomitant hemodynamic and electroencephalographic changes.
pseudosyncope.label: biology, medicine

pseudotensor.text: A quantity that transforms like a tensor under a proper rotation but gains an additional change of sign under an improper rotation.
pseudotensor.label: mathematics, physics

pseudoterminal.text: A pair of pseudodevices that can communicate with each other without the hardware that a true device would require.
pseudoterminal.label: computing

pseudothrombocytopenia.text: A spuriously lowered level of platelets.
pseudothrombocytopenia.label: medicine

pseudothrombophlebitis.text: The presence of signs and symptoms of phlebitis in the absence of a thrombophlebitis lesion.
pseudothrombophlebitis.label: medicine

pseudotolerance.text: A patient's requirement for an increased dose of a drug for reasons other than the patient's body having come to tolerate the existing dose.
pseudotolerance.label: pharmacology

pseudotolerant.text: Requiring an increased dose of a drug for reasons other than one's body having come to tolerate the existing dose.
pseudotolerant.label: pharmacology

pseudotorticollis.text: abnormal positioning of the head for ocular reasons
pseudotorticollis.label: medicine

pseudotrachea.text: One of the chitinous tubes found in the labella of dipterans (suborder Brachycera), used to carry liquid food into the mouth.
pseudotrachea.label: entomology, anatomy

pseudotriangle.text: Any subset of a plane that lies between any three mutually tangent convex sets
pseudotriangle.label: mathematics

pseudotriangulation.text: The partitioning of the plane into pseudotriangles
pseudotriangulation.label: mathematics

pseudotuberculosis.text: Any of several diseases that have the appearance of tuberculosis, but are caused by organisms other than Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
pseudotuberculosis.label: pathology

pseudotumor.text: An enlarged portion of tissue that resembles a tumor
pseudotumor.label: medicine

pseudotumor cerebri.text: A disease characterised by increased intracranial pressure of idiopathic aetiology, commonly affecting middle-aged women.
pseudotumor cerebri.label: medicine

pseudoturbinal.text: An incurved portion of the wall of the nasal chamber, distinguished from the true turbinals.
pseudoturbinal.label: anatomy

pseudotype.text: A viral vector having envelope proteins from two types of virus
pseudotype.label: biology

pseudotype.text: Something resembling, or having certain characteristics of, a data type.
pseudotype.label: computing

pseudoumbilical.text: Umbilical in the direction of the mean curvature vector field everywhere.
pseudoumbilical.label: mathematics

pseudounipolar.text: Of a neuron, having one axon that is split into two branches.
pseudounipolar.label: anatomy

pseudouridimycin.text: An antibiotic active against bacterial RNA polymerase
pseudouridimycin.label: medicine

pseudovalue.text: Something that resembles a value but is not a true value or does not really belong to the set of data being studied.
pseudovalue.label: mathematics, computing

pseudovariable.text: A named value that acts like a variable but is not a true variable.
pseudovariable.label: computing

pseudovariety.text: A class of algebras of a given signature, closed under the taking of homomorphic images, subalgebras and finitary direct products.
pseudovariety.label: mathematics

examples.text: Pseudovarieties are of particular importance in the study of finite semigroups and hence in formal language theory.

pseudovector.text: A quantity that transforms like a vector under a proper rotation but gains an additional change of sign under an improper rotation
pseudovector.label: mathematics, physics

pseudovirion.text: A synthetic viral particle that cannot replicate, used to inject foreign nucleic acid into a cell.
pseudovirion.label: virology

pseudowire.text: An emulation of a point-to-point connection over a packet-switching network.
pseudowire.label: computing, telecommunications

pseudoxanthoma.text: Any of several diseases of tendons and other tissues having some characteristics of true xanthomas
pseudoxanthoma.label: pathology

PSG.text: Initialism of Paris Saint-Germain Football Club, a French football club from Paris; from French PSG.
PSG.label: soccer

psi function.text: A function of a complex variable obtained by differentiating the logarithm of a gamma function; the digamma function
psi function.label: mathematics

psilosis.text: The sound change by which Greek lost the consonant sound /h/ during antiquity, h-dropping.
psilosis.label: phonology

psilosis.text: Sprue, a disease of the small intestine.
psilosis.label: medicine

PSIS.text: Initialism of posterior superior iliac spine.
PSIS.label: anatomy

psittacosis.text: An infection by Chlamydia bacteria, caught from infected birds, and characterised by fever, pneumonia and headaches.
psittacosis.label: pathology

psoas.text: Either of two muscles, the psoas major and psoas minor, involved in flexion of the trunk.
psoas.label: anatomy

psoas major.text: The psoas muscle involved in the flexion of the trunk and thigh.
psoas major.label: anatomy

psoas minor.text: The psoas muscle involved in the flexion of the trunk, specifically the lumbar vertebral column, located anterior to the psoas major.
psoas minor.label: anatomy

psoitis.text: Inflammation of a psoas muscle or its sheath.

ultrafilter.text: A proper filter which has a law of dichotomy for complements.
ultrafilter.label: mathematics, of a set, whose subsets are partially ordered by inclusion

examples.text: A proper filter of a set has these three properties: (1) it does not contain the empty set, (2) if it contains a subset then it contains all supersets of that subset, and (3) if it contains a pair of subsets then it also contains their intersection. To make it into an ultrafilter it must be made as large as possible without including the empty set. That can be prevented by not allowing any pair of disjoint sets to be both included. If, given a pair of complementary subsets, one of them is prevented from being included, then all subsets of it should be prevented from being included as well, by the second rule. That takes care of all subsets disjoint from the other complementary subset, which should then be included, in order to make the filter approach maximality, i.e., turn it into an ultrafilter.

ultrafilter.text: A filter (subset of a poset) that is maximal as a set with respect to the definition of proper filter.

examples.text: An ultrafilter is maximal in the sense that if any other element of the poset not already in it were added to it, one could deduce (from the laws which define the filter, and the given ordering relation, i.e., the structure of the poset) that the resulting filter must be improper; i.e., it must contain all the elements of the poset.

zygomaticus major.text: A slender band of muscle on each side of the face that arises from the zygomatic bone, inserts into the orbicularis oris and skin at the corner of the mouth, and acts to pull the corner of the mouth upward and backward when smiling or laughing.
zygomaticus major.label: anatomy

zygomaticus minor.text: A slender band of muscle on each side of the face that arises from the zygomatic bone, inserts into the upper lip between the zygomaticus major and the levator labii superioris, and acts to raise the upper lip upward and laterally.
zygomaticus minor.label: anatomy

zygomaxillary.text: Relating to the cheekbone and maxilla (upper jawbone).
zygomaxillary.label: anatomy

zygomectomy.text: Surgical removal or excision of the cheekbone.
zygomectomy.label: surgery

zygomycosis.text: An infection caused by bread mold fungi.
zygomycosis.label: pathology, mycology

zygon.text: In the cerebrum, a short crossbar fissure that connects the two pairs of branches of a larger zygal (H-shaped) fissure.
zygon.label: anatomy, plural "zyga"

zygon.text: An affinity or connection in a piece of music between tones, chords, or phrases, such that one part appears to repeat, to imitate, or to derive from the other, especially when perceived as an organising principle in the music; a zygonic relationship.
zygon.label: music, plural "zygons"

zygopodium.text: The radioulnar or tibiofibular portion of a tetrapod limb.
zygopodium.label: anatomy

zygopophysis.text: One of the articular processes of the neural arch of a vertebra
zygopophysis.label: anatomy

zygosphene.text: A median process on the front part of the neural arch of the vertebrae of most snakes and some lizards, which fits into a fossa called the zygantrum on the back part of the arch in front
zygosphene.label: anatomy

zymad.text: The organism responsible for a zymotic or infectious disease; the contagium vivum.
zymad.label: medicine

zymosthenic.text: Tending to strengthen the activity of an enzyme.
zymosthenic.label: medicine
